analysis.title: CIO Notebook: Democrats Sweep Congress
key_insights: Democrats took control of both the House and the Senate in the US midterms. They flipped 27 House seats so far and are on track for 40-45. They added seven Senate seats, with Alaska and Mississippi still too close to call.

Democrats won governorships in Texas, Ohio and Georgia and now hold the governor seat in all seven 2024 presidential swing states. Turnout skewed toward younger and female voters, and Latino voters and Independents shifted to Democrats.

Near term, Trump may push the lame duck Congress to address the debt ceiling (projected to be breached in February 2027) and raise defense spending. A Supreme Court nomination to replace Alito or Thomas is under discussion, though neither has announced retirement. Passage of these is likely hard given the Republican House losses and the short holiday window.
Permitting reform has bipartisan support and is more likely to pass in the coming weeks than the other lame duck initiatives.

In January the Democratic Congress is likely to push for restored ACA subsidies and Medicaid cuts reversal, lower pricing on more pharmaceutical drugs, a 10% cap on credit card interest, tariff relief on food, reversal of food stamp cuts and a housing affordability plan. Congress may also push for a resolution of the Iran conflict because additional funding needs approval.

If the debt ceiling is not raised in the lame duck session, Democrats may gain leverage on these proposals toward the second quarter of 2027. Faster congressional investigations make compromise hard, and Trump is expected to use his veto.

The most notable expected change is data center treatment. Voters showed discomfort through ballot questions and the governor results. Democrats are likely to review 100% expensing of data centers to slow their growth, and local taxes or costs could add to the recent inflationary impulse in data center inputs.
Power supply is already a constraint on data center build-out. The firm expects legal or financial restrictions on US data center growth to weigh on AI enablers.

Equity and bond markets reacted positively, a relief rally from lifted election uncertainty and recent downward pressure on data centers and AI. Higher interest rates, uncertain return on AI capital and Middle East tensions remain.
The firm is not making meaningful allocation changes. Given recent weakness in the AI trade, it sees possible opportunities in both equities and credit for investors with cash.

sector_views.rationale: Likely review of 100% expensing for data centers, plus legal or financial limits and power constraints, would slow US data center growth.
Democrats are expected to push for ACA subsidy restoration, Medicaid cut reversal and lower pricing on more drugs. The report gives no explicit stance.
